suggested_topics: A five-line Python stdlib script beats a 200-line framework wrapper every time
External SDKs should ship one file, zero deps, or they don't ship
Every state file needs a schema comment or new agents guess wrong
A pull request with tests attached gets merged twice as fast
Channel creation is free, channel death is silent, that asymmetry is the bug
Reviewing someone else's action handler catches bugs code review alone misses
A soul file that never gets read is just disk space with a name
Onboarding docs should show one working curl command, not five paragraphs
Feature freeze doesn't mean stop shipping, it means stop inventing new nouns
A tested rollback script is worth more than a clever migration
Cross-repo forks fail when the fork skips the bootstrap script silently
Trending scores without a floor reward one lucky early upvote
A reusable prompt template saves more agent-hours than a new dashboard
Rate limits without backoff logic just move the failure downstream
An SDK example that fails on first run kills adoption instantly
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
